import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

A **connector** is a fixed set of actions (search Gmail, comment on a PR, post to Slack) that call the vendor's real API. You connect a service once, usually through an OAuth consent screen, and its credentials are stored encrypted per tenant. Every agent in the workspace can then call it, either as an LLM tool or directly over REST. There are **18 built-in connectors**, counted from the executor's dispatch table ([`connector_executor.go`](repo:/blob/master/services/control-plane/internal/handlers/connector_executor.go)).

## Available connectors

| Area | Connector (`id`) | Actions | Credential |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Communication | Slack (`slack`) | list channels and users, post messages, reply in threads | OAuth or bot token |
| | Discord (`discord`) | list guilds, send messages | bot token or OAuth |
| | Telegram (`telegram`) | send messages, fetch updates | bot token |
| | Twilio (`twilio`) | send SMS, list messages, place calls, add conference participants | Account SID + Auth Token + phone number (or Messaging Service SID) |
| Email and calendar | Gmail (`gmail`) | list, search, send | Google OAuth or email + app password |
| | Google Calendar (`google-calendar`) | list and create events | Google OAuth |
| Docs and storage | Google Drive (`google-drive`) | list files | Google OAuth |
| | Google Sheets (`google-sheets`) | get a spreadsheet, get cell values | Google OAuth |
| | Notion (`notion`) | search, list databases | OAuth or integration token |
| Dev tools | GitHub (`github`) | list repos, list and get PRs and issues, create issues, comment on PRs | OAuth or personal access token |
| | Linear (`linear`) | list and create issues | API key or OAuth |
| | Jira (`jira`) | list and create issues | email + API token + domain, or OAuth |
| | Sentry (`sentry`) | list and get issues | auth token |
| | PagerDuty (`pagerduty`) | list and get incidents, create and update incidents, add notes | REST API key |
| | Vercel (`vercel`) | list projects and deployments | access token |
| CRM and sales | HubSpot (`hubspot`) | list contacts and deals | API key or OAuth |
| | Salesforce (`salesforce`) | run SOQL queries | access token + instance URL (OAuth supported) |
| Commerce | Stripe (`stripe`) | list charges and customers | secret key or OAuth |

<Aside>
**Web search** is a built-in tool, not a connector (sessions enable it with the `webSearch` flag). **Adding a connector** is a code change today: a new case in `connector_executor.go`. There is no plug-in interface.
</Aside>

## Connect one

1. Open **Integrations** (`/connectors`) in the dashboard.
2. For OAuth providers (Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Sheets, Slack, GitHub, Discord, Notion, Linear, Jira, HubSpot, Stripe, Salesforce), click the provider button, for example **Sign in with Google** or **Add to Slack**, and authorize. This works when the deployment has OAuth client credentials configured.
3. For key-based providers (Telegram, Twilio, Sentry, PagerDuty, Vercel), choose the manual option, for example **Enter bot token**, and fill in the credentials. They are tested before the connector shows as connected.

PagerDuty has no dashboard card yet; install it over the API (below). Uninstall with `DELETE /v1/connectors/{id}` to revoke access.

Credentials are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM when `PAL_CREDENTIAL_KEY` is set. Without it they are stored as plaintext, so set it outside dev. Credentials never appear in logs, traces or run state: connector actions run in the control plane, which resolves the credential at call time.

## Call an action

Call any action directly with `POST /v1/connectors/{id}/execute?action=<action>` and a JSON body of params. Install needs the `connectors:write` scope; `execute` needs `runs:execute`.

```bash
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/connectors/gmail/execute?action=search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "from:boss@company.com subject:urgent"}'
```

A successful call returns `{"connector", "action", "data"}`. A failed vendor call returns 502 with `{"error", "connector", "action"}`. An uninstalled connector returns 404 with a missing-credentials error naming it.

Agents get a curated subset of actions as tools (for example `github__list_prs`, `slack__post_message`, `gmail__search`) and decide when to call them. The full list is always callable over REST and from workflow connector nodes.

### Newer actions

| Connector / action | Params | Credential (config field) | Class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `slack` / `reply_thread` | `channel`, `text`, `thread_ts` (all required) | OAuth, or `botToken` | write |
| `github` / `comment_pr` | `owner`, `repo`, `number`, `body` (all required) | OAuth, or `personalAccessToken` | write |
| `sentry` / `get_issue` | `organization`, `issue_id` (required) | `authToken` | read-only |
| `google-calendar` / `create_event` | `summary`, `start`, `end` (required, RFC3339); optional `calendarId` (default `primary`), `timeZone`, `description`, `location`, `attendees` (array of emails) | Google OAuth | write |
| `pagerduty` / `list_incidents` | optional `status` (`triggered`, `acknowledged`, `resolved`), `limit` (default 25) | `apiKey` | read-only |
| `pagerduty` / `get_incident` | `incident_id` (required) | `apiKey` | read-only |
| `pagerduty` / `create_incident` | `title`, `service_id`, `from` (required; `from` is the acting user's email); optional `details` | `apiKey` | write |
| `pagerduty` / `update_incident` | `incident_id`, `from`, `status` (required; `acknowledged` or `resolved`) | `apiKey` | write |
| `pagerduty` / `add_note` | `incident_id`, `content`, `from` (all required) | `apiKey` | write |

Slack `post_message` also accepts an optional `thread_ts`; `reply_thread` is the same call with `thread_ts` required. PagerDuty agents get `list_incidents` and `get_incident` as tools. `create_incident`, `update_incident` and `add_note` are REST-only, plus usable from workflow connector nodes.

```bash
# install PagerDuty (config.apiKey = a REST API key)
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/connectors/install \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"connectorId": "pagerduty", "displayName": "PagerDuty", "config": {"apiKey": "..."}}'

# read an incident
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/connectors/pagerduty/execute?action=get_incident" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"incident_id": "PABC123"}'

# acknowledge it (write; "from" is required by PagerDuty)
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/connectors/pagerduty/execute?action=update_incident" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"incident_id": "PABC123", "from": "oncall@example.com", "status": "acknowledged"}'

# reply in a Slack thread
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/connectors/slack/execute?action=reply_thread" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel": "C0123", "thread_ts": "1700000000.000100", "text": "On it."}'
```

## Read-only versus side-effecting

PAL Runtime keeps an explicit allowlist of read-only actions in `connector_safety.go` (for example `list_*`, `get_*`, `search` and `query` on the built-in connectors). Every other action, including any action on an unknown connector, counts as side-effecting. In the workflow engine, [confidence gating](/docs/pal/human-in-the-loop/) (off by default) can route side-effecting steps to a human first.

## Which agents can use a connector

Connectors are installed per workspace, not per agent. Once connected, every agent in the workspace can call it. The agent page's Connectors card is a read-only list linking to `/connectors`. To limit the blast radius, use [budget](/docs/build/budgets/) `toolLimits` (workflow tool and connector nodes only), the approval and confidence gates, or a separate workspace.

OAuth scopes come from `oauth_providers.go`. Gmail asks for `gmail.modify` (read, send, label; no permanent delete), GitHub for `repo` and `read:user`, Slack for `channels:read`, `chat:write` and `users:read`.

## Test without a vendor account

Point a vendor at a local fixture server. This is dev and test only.

1. Start the fixture server from `services/control-plane`. It listens on loopback and serves recorded responses for Slack, GitHub, Sentry, PagerDuty and Google Calendar.

   ```bash
   go run ./cmd/connector-replay            # 127.0.0.1:9191
   go run ./cmd/connector-replay -addr 127.0.0.1:9292
   ```

2. Point the control plane at it before starting it. `PAL_ENV` must not be `prod`, `production` or `staging`.

   ```bash
   export PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_SLACK=http://127.0.0.1:9191
   export PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_GITHUB=http://127.0.0.1:9191
   export PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_SENTRY=http://127.0.0.1:9191
   export PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_GOOGLE=http://127.0.0.1:9191
   export PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_PAGERDUTY=http://127.0.0.1:9191
   make run-api
   ```

3. Install a connector with any non-empty token, execute an action, then read what the server saw:

   ```bash
   curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9191/__requests
   ```

   Each recorded call has `method`, `path`, `query`, `header`, `body`, `hasAuth`, `matched` and `status`. The `Authorization` header is never stored, only whether it was set.

| Variable | Vendor host replaced | Connectors affected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_SLACK` | `slack.com` | Slack |
| `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_GITHUB` | `api.github.com` | GitHub |
| `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_SENTRY` | `sentry.io` | Sentry |
| `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_GOOGLE` | `www.googleapis.com` | Google Calendar, Google Drive |
| `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_PAGERDUTY` | `api.pagerduty.com` | PagerDuty |

The value must be an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host. Only scheme and host are replaced; the vendor path is kept. An unmatched request gets 404 with `{"error": "no recorded fixture for METHOD PATH"}`.

Fixtures are exact method + path matches in `internal/connectorreplay/fixtures.json`, embedded in the binary: Slack `conversations.list` and `chat.postMessage`; GitHub `acme/api` pulls list, PR 42, and a comment on 42; Sentry org `acme` issues list and issue `1001`; PagerDuty incidents list, get `PABC123`, create, update; Google Calendar `primary` events list and insert. Use those owner, repo, org and ids in your test params.

## Limits

- **Overrides are refused in production.** With `PAL_ENV` set to `prod`, `production` or `staging`, the control plane exits if any `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_*` variable is set, because a bearer token must never go to an arbitrary host. The outbound transport also ignores overrides in prod at request time. A malformed value is fatal in every environment.
- **No plug-in interface.** A new connector is a code change.
- **Workspace-wide access.** There is no per-agent connector assignment.
